_comment: P-TQA.7 — accepted/pre-existing high+critical advisories. The audit gate (scripts/auditGate.mjs) BLOCKS any high/critical NOT listed here. Each entry is triaged: dev-only, no safe fix, or a separate upgrade task. Re-triage periodically and remove once fixed. A NEW high/critical in any other package fails CI.

allow.reason: dev-only test runner (not shipped to users); fix requires a major-version bump tracked as a separate task.
dev-only coverage tool (P-TQA.1); same advisory as vitest (via: vitest) — fix is a semver-major vitest 4 upgrade tracked with the vitest entry. Never shipped to users.
dev/build-only toolchain (not shipped at runtime); upgrade tracked separately to avoid a risky major bump.
pre-existing transitive; upgrade evaluated separately (used server-side; needs regression check before bumping).
payments SDK; vendor-pinned — upgrade requires payment-flow re-verification, tracked separately.
transitive (fetch/runtime); pre-existing, upgrade tracked separately.
no upstream fix available on npm (prototype-pollution/ReDoS advisories); usage is server-side and input-controlled — tracked separately.

GHSA (RSC-mode CSRF bypass, range >=7.12.0 <8.3.0) applies ONLY to React Router's RSC/server-action mode; NavBharatAI is a Vite SPA using client-side routing (no RSC), so it is not exploitable. The only npm 'fix' is a breaking v8 major (>=8.3.0) or a downgrade to <7.12.0 which REINTRODUCES the 7.18.0-patched DoS (GHSA-chx6-hx7r-mcp5). Pinned at 7.18.1 (DoS-patched); v8 migration tracked separately.
Same advisory as react-router (via react-router). RSC-mode-only CSRF, not applicable to our SPA. Pinned at 7.18.1 (DoS-patched); v8 upgrade is a breaking major, tracked separately.

GHSA-mh99-v99m-4gvg (DoS via unbounded expansion), fixed only in 5.0.8. Root-caused and attempted a `package.json` overrides pin to 5.0.8 (2026-07-25) — reverted because 5.0.8 changed its CJS export shape and broke the legacy minimatch bundled inside glob (used by @vitest/coverage-v8's test-exclude → glob chain): `brace_expansion_1.default is not a function`, a real CI failure, not a hypothetical. Every reachable instance is transitive-only via dev/CLI tooling (firebase-tools, vitest coverage) — never imported in src/, never shipped, never run against user-supplied input (only against our own trusted repo paths/config globs). True fix needs glob's bundled minimatch (inside test-exclude/coverage-v8) and firebase-tools' vendored minimatch to publish a brace-expansion@5.x-compatible release; tracked as an open root cause, revisit periodically.

Same brace-expansion cascade (glob's bundled minimatch, and the copy vendored inside firebase-tools). Dev-only (firebase-tools CLI / vitest coverage), never shipped, never reachable by users. See brace-expansion entry above for the full root-cause note.
Same brace-expansion/minimatch cascade. Dev-only: only reached via firebase-tools (CLI) and test-exclude (vitest coverage tooling). Never shipped, never reachable by users.

Aggregates the brace-expansion/minimatch/glob cascade in its own dependency tree. devDependency only (the Firebase deploy CLI) — never imported in src/, never bundled into the shipped app or server. npm's suggested 'fix' is a downgrade to 14.23.0 (a semver-major regression, not an upgrade); the real fix is upstream (firebase-tools needs to update its vendored glob/minimatch to a brace-expansion@5.x-compatible version). Tracked as an open root cause.
